_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: [Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. Two commits reviewed. 4e3b223 changes which exception MailConnectionProbe throws when the server rejects a login: MailAuthenticationException instead of MailConnectionException, so the reply text stops being rendered into the user-facing error.mail.connectionFailed placeholder and travels as the cause into the log instead. That narrows what server-controlled text reaches the UI; it touches no TLS, auth-mechanism or timeout setting. Re-checked on the probe specifically: pinned ssl.checkserveridentity, the fail-closed OAuth2-requires-SSL guard and the millisecond-string timeouts are all unchanged. 5c76f91 adds an outbound content type: MimeMessageBuilder attaches a text/html alternative rendered by the new MarkdownBodyRenderer when the composed body uses Markdown. The HTML is generated locally from the user's own keystrokes, never from server-controlled data, so the hostile-server surface this boundary is about is untouched — as are TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path. Re-checked the send path specifically: the CRLF guard on header-bound fields (requireSingleLine) and both AddressPolicy branches are unchanged, and drafts stay single-part text/plain, so the IMAP APPEND payload shape is identical to what was audited. The renderer runs with escapeHtml and sanitizeUrls on and HtmlBlock parsing off, so it cannot emit script, event handlers or non-http/mailto URLs; rendering is skipped above 512 kB, below the existing 10 MB body cap, so it adds no unbounded CPU sink to the send path. Verdict stays PASS. Third commit reviewed: the conversation-scope change adds FolderRole.SENT to CONVERSATION_EXCLUDED_ROLES in MailFacade, which under this path is two functional lines (the role list and a log string) plus javadoc. It moves nothing this boundary is about: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently — the change decides which folders a read-path query counts. Two effects re-checked because they do reach IMAP. (1) The listing now resolves a fourth folder role per page, through the same bounded findFolderNamesByRoleWithoutWaiting call the other three already used, with the same fail-closed handling: an unresolvable role still degrades the whole listing to folder-scoped rather than guessing an exclusion set. (2) The resolved names are attacker-controlled (the server names its folders) and now include the sent folder, but they ride the same :excludedFolders JPQL parameter binding as before, so the NOT IN clause gains a value, not a new injection surface; the list stays bounded by the folders the server reports for those roles, which was already true of trash, junk and drafts. Verdict stays PASS. Fourth commit reviewed: the setext-heading fix in MarkdownBodyRenderer. It renders strictly less, not more — a paragraph followed by a --- or === rule used to become a heading and is now demoted back to a paragraph, so bodies that only tripped that rule no longer produce an HTML alternative at all. Input is unchanged in kind: the composed body, the user's own keystrokes, never server-controlled bytes, so the hostile-server surface this boundary is about is untouched, as are TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path. Re-checked the three things that could have moved. (1) The re-appended underline is taken from the source body and inserted as a Text node, so it goes through the same escapeHtml pass as any other text — it cannot introduce markup, and sanitizeUrls and the HtmlBlock-off setting are unchanged. (2) includeSourceSpans(BLOCKS) was added to the parser purely to tell ATX from setext; comparing parse trees with and without it confirmed it does not change parsing, only annotates blocks. (3) No new unbounded work in the send path: the tree walk is linear in nodes, and the one added allocation (splitting the body into lines) happens only when a setext heading was actually found, still under the existing 512 kB render cap. Drafts remain single-part text/plain, so the IMAP APPEND payload shape is still what was audited. Verdict stays PASS. Same review extended to the follow-up in that commit: ENABLED_BLOCKS moved from Set.of to an explicitly ordered LinkedHashSet. This removes nondeterminism rather than adding behaviour — CommonMark registers block parsers in iteration order and Set.of salts that order per JVM, so the renderer produced different documents for the same body between runs (six runs of one parse: five headings, one thematic break). The set contains the same five block types as before, so no parser is added or removed and no new construct becomes renderable; only the tie-break between heading and thematic break for a rule under a paragraph is now fixed instead of random. Nothing here reaches TLS, auth, timeouts or any IMAP command path, and the inbound parsing this boundary is about uses MimePartExtractor, not this renderer. Verdict stays PASS. Fifth commit reviewed: the thread-position fix, whose whole diff under this path is one file, ThreadingService.java. attachToExistingThread stops assigning max(threadPosition) + 1 and instead appends only when a COUNT reports that nothing in the thread sorts after the arrival, renumbering the thread otherwise through the same pass reconcileLateArrivingParent already used. Nothing this boundary is about moves: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently — In-Reply-To, References and the subject normalization feed the same lookups as before, and the References walk keeps its MAX_REFERENCES_WALK cap. The one thing that could have moved a verdict is resource use on the sync path, which is what B1-1 and B1-2 were both about, so it was weighed rather than waved through. The renumbering pass loads a thread's members as managed entities, @Lob bodies included, so a hostile server drip-feeding a large thread in descending date order could make each arrival re-read the whole thread: quadratic in thread length, with the bodies in the heap. That exposure is not new and its worst case is unchanged — the same pass already ran on every orphan merge, and on an initial sync those dominate, because MessageDownloader walks UIDs newest-first, so a reply is threaded before its parent and reaches the merge branch rather than this one. The new branch fires only for an arrival that is both older than an existing member and already has a mirrored parent, which that same newest-first walk makes the exception rather than the rule. The COUNT that decides it is bounded and served by the existing (account_id, thread_id) index. Recorded as a known cost rather than closed: teaching the renumber to read a body-free projection would remove the heap term from both call sites and is worth its own change. Verdict stays PASS. Sixth commit reviewed: 4d3f6d6, a dead-code and javadoc cleanup whose entire non-comment diff under this path is five lines — spelled out here because the check compares tree ids and cannot tell a comment from code. MailSyncService loses getMessageOrThrow, a @Transactional(readOnly = true) repository lookup that had no caller since the initial import, together with its now-unused ResourceNotFoundException import; downloadRange changes from public to private. Everything else under the path (ImapActionService, ImapCapabilities, MessageFetcher) is javadoc text, verified by filtering the diff to lines that are neither comment nor blank. Nothing this boundary is about moves: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool entry or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently. The two things that could have moved a verdict were checked. (1) The deleted method removes no reachable behaviour — it read a message by stableId and threw when absent, and the read paths that do this go through MessageService.getByStableId, which is unchanged, so no error surface and no exception-to-ProblemDetail mapping moves. (2) The visibility narrowing removes an entry point rather than adding one: downloadRange assumes the per-folder lock that its only caller, syncAndBackfill, already holds, so private makes that locking discipline unforgeable from outside instead of leaving it to convention — the same direction as the Store-containment rule ArchitectureTest enforces. The three javadoc fixes correct names that had gone stale (the post-send draft cleanup is SmtpMessageService.sendDraft doing a hard delete, not a MailFacade move-to-trash) and record why ImapCapabilities.hasQresync is unused; they change no behaviour this audit weighs. Verdict stays PASS. That commit was then extended with an unused-import removal, which moves this tree again, so the id above is the later one. The incremental change under this path is three lines, all of them imports: MailSyncService drops Transactional and MessageEntity, orphaned by the getMessageOrThrow deletion in the same commit, and MimeMessageBuilder drops an unused AddressException. Verified as the complete diff between the two revisions for this path, not sampled. No executable statement, annotation or type reference moves, and the compiler is a second witness — an import that was actually load-bearing would not have built. Nothing this boundary is about is touched: TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path are unchanged, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently. Worth recording for whoever reviews this path next: nothing in the build reports an unused import, because Spotless here deliberately omits removeUnusedImports (it does not yet support JEP 511 import module, per the note in pom.xml), so this class of leftover accumulates silently and its presence is not evidence that anything else drifted. Verdict stays PASS. Third commit, the dead-code batch: the whole diff under this path is MessageDownloader.getLatestUidFromServer going public -> private plus the javadoc saying why (its only caller, syncNewMessages, is in the same class and the value only means something next to that caller lastUid comparison). No statement inside the body changed, so UIDNEXT handling, the UID sweep and every IMAP call sequence the audit traces are byte-identical; narrowing visibility can only remove a way to reach the method, never add one, and nothing outside the class reached it. Verdict PASS stands. Java caller gate batch, four files under mail/service and one util. Additions are javadoc only: a @callerless tag on ImapCapabilities.hasQresync and on the package-private emitter count in SseNotificationService. Deletions are two methods nothing called: SyncLockManager.isSyncing (a read-only view of the lock set; tryLock/unlock, the methods the sync path actually uses, are untouched) and SyncStateService.saveSyncState (the entity-wide save; every hot-path write goes through the targeted update* methods, which are unchanged). MimePartExtractor loses the uncalled extractText wrapper. No IMAP or SMTP call sequence, no lock ordering and no connection handling moved. Verdict PASS stands. Scheduler default batch, two files under mail/service and not a single statement inside either method body. MailSyncScheduler.syncAccounts and SseNotificationService.sendHeartbeat lose the inline fallbacks from their @Scheduled placeholders (:PT5M, :PT10S, :PT30S); the rest of the diff is the comment saying why they are gone. All three keys already carry a default on the SyncProperties component that binds them, so each value had two defaults in two syntaxes that nothing reconciled. Nothing this boundary is about moves: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, socket timeout (those are ImapProperties/SmtpProperties, untouched), connection-pool entry or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently. The two things that could have moved a verdict were checked rather than waved through. (1) The operative values are unchanged, so the sync cadence this audit weighed under B1-1 and B1-2 is identical: application.properties sets interval=5m, initial-delay=10s and sse-heartbeat-interval=30s, the same durations the removed fallbacks spelled as PT5M, PT10S and PT30S. Verified by running it, not by reading the file — with a key commented out the context refuses to start and names the placeholder, which is also the proof that the inline fallback was the only other source and that the record @DefaultValue never reaches a placeholder. (2) The failure mode moves fail-closed, not open: a missing key used to leave the scheduler running at a rate nobody chose, and now stops startup. That can only reduce unintended IMAP traffic, never increase it. Verdict PASS stands.

Comment-only change under this path. 578526c moves the @callerless waiver on ImapCapabilities.hasQresync and SseNotificationService.getActiveEmitterCount out of javadoc into a line comment, because @callerless is not a javadoc tag and Error Prone rejected all five of the gate’s waivers with InvalidBlockTag. Verified line by line rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path is a comment line — a javadoc opener, closer or continuation going out, a // coming in. No statement, signature, annotation or literal changed, so no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool policy or IMAP command path moved, and no server-controlled byte reaches anywhere it did not before. The waiver text itself is unchanged in substance: the QRESYNC probe is still recorded and still unused, which is the fact the waiver exists to state. Verdict stays PASS.

API-equivalence and comment-only change under this path. fa1333f swaps six `get(0)` / `get(size() - 1)` calls here for `getFirst()` / `getLast()` (ImapFolderService, MailFacade, MarkdownBodyRenderer, ThreadingBackfillService, ThreadingService twice), replaces `Thread.sleep(millis)` with the `Duration` overload in DraftPersistenceService, and adds comments — nothing else — at the folder-close sites in ImapFolderExecutor, ImapAppendService (two) and ImapActionService. Verified line by line rather than by intent: every changed line is either a comment or a call whose replacement is specified in terms of the call it replaces, so no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool policy, IMAP command path or MIME parse step moved, and no server-controlled byte reaches anywhere it did not before. The sequenced accessors differ from the indexed ones only in the exception thrown on an empty list (NoSuchElementException rather than IndexOutOfBoundsException), and each of the six sites is guarded by an emptiness check that makes the empty case unreachable, so no new failure mode reaches a caller. The added comments state why those closes must stay `close(false)` / `close(mode == READ_WRITE)` and must not become try-with-resources — the inherited no-arg Folder.close() is close(true), i.e. expunge — which records the behaviour the audit already verified instead of changing it. Verdict stays PASS.

Documentation and idiom change under these paths. 7ec2793 adds the javadoc summary sentences Error Prone was asking for (ImapProperties, DraftPersistenceService.prepareDraftIdentity, SmtpMessageService.sendEmailAsync), reattaches the ImapFolderService javadoc that had come loose from findFolderNamesByRole and was documenting nothing, annotates ThreadingService.renumberThreadPositions with @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") where the identity compare is already explained in its own javadoc, and swaps two Collections.emptyList() for List.of() in the MailDraftService reply and forward drafts. Verified line by line: every changed line is a comment, an annotation, or an empty-list factory call that yields an immutable empty list either way. No TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool policy, IMAP command path or MIME parse step moved. Verdict stays PASS.

(1) The install path is unchanged: both buttons still call postponePromptedUpdate and installPromptedUpdate and both still carry disabled={installing}, so an install in flight still cannot be re-triggered or postponed from here. The design-system sweep touches this path in one file, AboutSettings.svelte, and the whole commit diff for it is a single line: the status dot's dotClass moves from the raw Tailwind bg-emerald-500 to the new bg-success token. That dot belongs to notificationStatus, the SSE connection indicator, and not to the update check — the update surface in this file is byte-identical (the checkForUpdateManually import, handleCheckForUpdates, updateCheckStatus and the channel selector), as are the other twelve Code paths entries, so the endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are untouched, and so is the manual-check failure UI with its RELEASES_URL fallback that §5 rests on. windows-signed-release.yml gains one step, 'Verify updater signature against the shipped pubkey', between manifest generation and Authenticode verification. It is additive in the only direction that matters: it runs the new frontend/scripts/verify-updater-signature.mjs, which reads the generated tauri.release.conf.json and latest.json and fails the build when the installer's minisign signature does not verify against the pubkey that build ships. Nothing else in the workflow moves — verified as a diff that adds a step and a comment and changes no existing line, so the fail-closed secret validation, the config-prep invocation, the bundle build, the attestation and the publish logic are byte-identical, and the other twelve Code paths entries are unchanged. The trust chain is untouched by construction: the gate only reads artifacts and can only turn a green build red, so no path it guards can become more permissive. The verdict does not move (PASS), but the audit text now understates the pipeline: §2 claims a fail-closed build and sign pipeline while listing only that a missing pubkey or endpoint aborts the build, and the key-pair check it lacked is precisely what this step adds. Recorded here rather than rewritten into the audit because the queued B6 revision (todo.md, 'Nalezy z revize updateru') also has to take in the script-injection surface of both workflows and add the new script to Code paths; splitting that across two passes would mean two version bumps for one review.

Installing an update stops the backend sidecar first, which needed a seam between downloading and installing, so lib.rs gains one command (download_pending_update) and install_pending_update now installs bytes the previous call left in managed state. Read for the two ways that could weaken the boundary, and it does neither. (1) Signature verification is unmoved: Update::download verifies against the pinned pubkey before it returns the buffer, and Update::install does not re-check, so the requirement is that the verified bytes never leave Rust — they do not. DownloadedUpdate is managed state like PendingUpdate, the webview receives no bytes and passes none back, and the command signatures carry only a version string. Routing the package through the renderer is the shape that would have broken this, and it was rejected for exactly that reason (recorded in the doc comment on DownloadedUpdate). (2) The expected-version pin is now applied twice rather than once: take_expected_update re-checks the pending slot on both calls, and install additionally compares the downloaded package's own version, because a check landing between the two calls moves the pending slot while the bytes stay behind. check_for_update clears the downloaded package for the same reason. Channel routing, beta_endpoint_override, the capability set (still no updater: permission), tauri.conf.json and the CSP are byte-identical. On the frontend, updates.ts gains the download call and the sidecar shutdown between the two invokes; the failure path restarts the backend through bootstrap. The install guard was also narrowed from 'available' or 'installing' to 'available' only — with a download in front of the install, the old shape admitted a second run that would have started a second download. Verdict stays PASS. What the next B6 revision must fix rather than acknowledge: §1's enumeration of the IPC surface is now stale twice over. It names two commands where there are three, and it already said 'the install command takes no arguments' when install_pending_update has taken expectedVersion since v1.2. The revision is queued in todo.md together with the workflow injection surface and the new verify-updater-signature.mjs, which belongs under Code paths.

[Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. 3c2e1b3 touches this path in documentation only: ConversationSummaryResponse gains a reworded record javadoc and a reworded @Schema description for messageCount, because the conversation scope stopped spanning the sent folder. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no validation annotation was touched — so none of the things this audit weighs (request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes) moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for the commit is a single description string, and the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by exactly the one @description comment line that carries it — no type, field name or optionality in the generated client surface moves. Verdict stays PASS. — 9567d49 moves the address book out of the account scope: the contact endpoints go from /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts and .../contact-labels to /api/v1/contacts and /api/v1/contact-labels, and both controllers lose their accountId path variable (autocomplete keeps it as a @RequestParam @Positive). Nothing this audit weighs moves with them. Authorization is path-independent: SecurityConfig permits only PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (the OAuth callbacks) and leaves anyRequest().authenticated() behind ApiKeyFilter, so a relocated path keeps the same posture — there is no per-prefix rule to fall out of. The two counts the enumeration rests on are unchanged (17 @RestController, 12 @Validated): no controller was added, removed, or stripped of @Validated. Every bound §2 cites is untouched — bulk 100 items, merge 9 sources / 10 emails, label assignment 100 contacts / 50 labels, label name 60 chars, contactQueryMaxLength and the contactAutocompleteMaxLimit clamp — and the whole contact/dto diff for this commit is a single javadoc line; account/dto only gains @Nullable on MailProviderResponse.oauth2RegistrationId, which springdoc does not read, so the golden api-docs.json does not move for it. Error hygiene is unchanged in shape: the contact exceptions drop their accountId argument and still resolve through AppException to an RFC 9457 ProblemDetail. The audit enumerates no endpoint paths, so the move leaves no stale claim. Verdict stays PASS. — 472de85 touches this path in documentation only: the ThreadResponse record javadoc drops the hedge that threadPosition order matches receivedAt ascending only for the canonical case, because ThreadingService now places every arrival by its own receivedAt instead of appending it. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no @Schema description or validation annotation was touched, so none of the things this audit weighs — request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes — moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json does not appear in the commit diff at all and OpenApiSnapshotTest passes, so the generated client surface cannot have moved either; springdoc reads @Schema, not record javadoc. What changed is the truth of a claim the endpoint already made about its own ordering, not the shape of what it returns. Verdict stays PASS. — The vCard-import fix touches this path in one file, BulkContactCreateRequest.java, and only above the record header: a class javadoc now says what the 100-item cap is for. Verified as a comment-only diff, every changed line inside the added /** */ block; the record component and its @NotEmpty / @Size(max = 100) / @Valid annotations are byte-identical, so every bound this audit rests on in §2 is the one that was audited. No @Schema was added, so the generated surface cannot move either — springdoc reads annotations, not javadoc, and the golden api-docs.json is absent from the commit diff with OpenApiSnapshotTest green. The comment records why the cap exists (it bounds the per-item transactions of one request, not its bytes) and points at finding A1 for the byte question, which is a restatement of what §2 and §6 already establish, not a new claim. Verdict stays PASS. Dead-code batch: the whole diff under core/security is the deletion of InternalApiKeyProvider.invalidateCache, a method with no caller anywhere in main or test. ApiKeyFilter -- the component this audit reasons about, and the only reader of the provider -- is byte-identical, and so is getKey and the AtomicReference it memoizes; HandshakeService mints the key once per process and has no rotation path, which is why nothing ever called the invalidation. Removing an uncalled method cannot change which requests the filter accepts. Verdict PASS stands.

Verdict stays PASS. 4d3f6d6 touches this path in comments only — verified by filtering the commit diff to lines that are neither comment nor blank, which comes back empty; the whole change is javadoc on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken. One idiom change under this path. 7ec2793 rewrites both cache lookups in OAuth2TokenService.getAccessToken from "cached.isPresent() && cached.get().isFresh()" to tokenCache.get(accountId).filter(CachedToken::isFresh). Optional.filter evaluates the predicate only when a value is present, exactly as the && short-circuit did, and the cache is still read once per lookup, so the freshness decision, the double-check under the refresh lock and the fall-through to doRefresh all behave as before. No token is cached, logged or transmitted differently, and no scope, redirect URI or PKCE handling is in the diff. Verdict stays PASS.
